title: Keeping in touch
grammar: Asking questions in the present simple · email writing

scene.speaker: nova
scene.bubble: Read Liam's email to his new pen-friend, learn how to ask good questions, then write your own.
scene.intro: Part of the Inspiring Nordic project is meeting new people. This term every student has a pen-friend from another school. In this unit you read a real email from Liam to his pen-friend Sam, you learn how to ask good questions in the present simple, and you write a friendly email of your own. A good email tells about you and asks about the other person — so let's learn to keep in touch.

activities.title: Reading — an email to a pen-friend

data.author: liam
data.title: Hi from Nordic!
data.byline: an email from Liam to Sam
data.text:
Hi Sam,

Thanks for your email — it's great to have a pen-friend! My name is Liam and I'm in Grade 6 at Nordic School in Peru.

I love sport, especially football. I play every day after school with my friends, and at the weekend I watch matches on TV with my cousin. I'm also in the reading club now. This term our class is reading Charlie and the Chocolate Factory — it's really funny, and Willy Wonka is my favourite character.

My family is quite big. I live with my mum, my dad, my two sisters and our dog, Rocky. My best friend, Mateo, lives next door, so we walk to school together.

What about you? What do you do in your free time? Do you have any pets? Please write back soon and tell me all about your school.

Best wishes,
Liam

data.title: Asking questions (present simple)
data.intro: In an email to a new friend, we ask questions. In the present simple, we make questions with do and does.

examples.text: What do you do in your free time?

rules: Make present simple questions with do (I / you / we / they) and does (he / she / it).
After do / does, use the base verb with no -s: Does he play? (not plays).
With be, put the verb first: What's your name? Are you from Peru?

activities.title: Speaking — meet a pen-friend. Role-play in pairs, then record it.

data.text: Role-play meeting a new pen-friend. Model: “Where do you study?” — “I study at Nordic School. What about you?”  Student A asks four questions: What's your name? Where do you study? What do you do in your free time? Do you have any pets? Student B answers in full sentences, then you swap. Record your best conversation.

homework.prompt: Write a friendly email (6–7 sentences) to a new pen-friend for the Inspiring Nordic project. Start with 'Dear ___,' and end with 'Best wishes'. Tell them your name and class, one hobby, the book your class is reading, and ask them two questions. Capital letters and full stops!

outcomes.puede: Catch the key points of a class announcement about the pen-friend project (A2 Key Listening).
Ask and answer present simple questions to meet a new friend (A2 Key Speaking Part 1).
Read an informal email and find the main idea and the details (A2 Key Reading).
Write a friendly email with 'Dear…' and 'Best wishes', telling about myself and asking questions.
Asking questions with do / does and be; words for letters and emails.
